item.nusmp.snugglable_doll.desc: A stitched blue cat with button eyes and a ghost grinning behind it. It brings Snuggles to life, a hardier cat that fights at your side, and lends you Telepathy to speak with it.
item.nusmp.paralyzing_perfume.card:
Rare Grade charm. Spray this in an enemy's face to paralyze them. One perfume bottle holds about 10 uses.
Spray (3 second cooldown, one charge). A cloud sprays up to five blocks in front of you in a half-cone: every foe in it must make a DC 17 Constitution save (d20 + 1 per 25 maximum health, at most +8; a creature of 400 health or more cannot be held). Those who fail are paralyzed for 18 seconds (Tensura's Paralysis; Slowness and Weakness if Tensura's effect is absent), 3 seconds only for players.
The bottle holds 10 charges and one comes back at every dawn.
Tabletop made game: 3 turns became 18 seconds; the Constitution save became the d20 roll above; "10 uses and then nothing" became 10 charges that slowly refill.
item.nusmp.paralyzing_perfume.desc: Spray it in a foe's face to hold them still for a few seconds unless they shake it off. Ten sprays in the bottle; one comes back at every dawn.
item.nusmp.satchel_of_unmet_needs.card:
Special Grade charm. This bag resembles a Bag of Holding but resists any attempt to place objects into it; it weighs about 20 pounds despite appearing empty and rattles when shaken. On the underside of the flap is a message: "Sleen temnur uoyro fedivor pot tub dlohot tsixet onodi."
Choose Object (use it to go down the list): pen and ink, bedroll, crowbar, bell, empty bottles, rope, chain, lock and key, lantern, bucket, iron pot, tinderbox, magnifying glass, steel mirror, ten-foot pole, folded tent, and (added, the card's list is cut off) torches and rations.
Reach In. Pulls the chosen object out of the bag. A second of the same object cannot be produced while the first still exists. An object left outside the bag for a game day (or destroyed) vanishes into thin air and is missing from the bag until three dawns have passed.
Put Back. The chosen object goes back into the bag at once and can be called again.
Tabletop made game: each real-world tool became the nearest Minecraft item; "24 hours" is one game day; the object is found by a mark on the item.
item.nusmp.satchel_of_unmet_needs.desc: A satchel that cannot be stocked, only emptied: choose an object, reach in and pull it out. It vanishes after a day outside the bag, and is then missing for three dawns.
item.nusmp.drow_sunscreen.card:
Special Grade charm. Use this handy sunscreen to protect your sensitive Underdark skin from the sun's harmful rays! Don't forget to reapply!
Apply Sunscreen (three uses a game day). For three game hours (3000 ticks): burning damage you take under the open sky in daylight is halved, and blindness, darkness and flash-blindness are lifted from you every second.
Tabletop made game: "immune to sun sensitivity" became a daylight fire and gloom shield (Minecraft has no sun sensitivity for players; Tensura races that burn by day feel it).
item.nusmp.drow_sunscreen.desc: Protect your sensitive Underdark skin from the sun. Three hours after applying, the sun's burn is halved and flashes and gloom cannot blind you. Don't forget to reapply!
item.nusmp.portable_god.card:
Rare Grade charm. Requires attunement (worshipping a certain god). A little figure that pictures a certain god. It holds 12 charges; three come back at every dawn (the card's "loses its magic" became a slow refill).
Punishment (1 charge). The creature you look at (within 24 blocks) takes a d10 of damage.
Rescue (2 charges). You, or the friend you look at, gain temporary hit points (absorption) worth a d10.
Holy Spirit (3 charges). Your next melee blow within a minute carries an extra d10.
Revenge (4 charges). For a minute, the first creature that hits you takes 3d10 in return.
Deus Ex (5 charges). For a minute you are the avatar: every melee blow carries an extra d10, you gain Resistance and you shine.
Wonder (7 charges). The wild magic table, d100: ten rows (fire burst, lightning on your target, healing wave, levitation, speed and haste, shielding, invisibility with night vision, the god's laughter, a shock wave, a boon of strength and resistance) and a hundred is a WISH: full health, negative effects lifted, regeneration, resistance, strength and a shield.
Tabletop made game: damage types became plain magic (the pictured god is yours); "bonus action" and "reaction" became armed states that spend themselves on the next blow dealt or taken.
item.nusmp.portable_god.desc: A little figure of your god with twelve charges (three return at dawn): Punishment, Rescue, Holy Spirit, Revenge, Deus Ex and Wonder, each at its own price.
item.nusmp.jar_of_bats.card:
Rare Grade charm. Break or open the jar to release a swarm of bats controlled by whomever holds it.
Release the Swarm (2% mana, 3 minute cooldown). Six bats swarm out and answer only to you for a minute: every second they fall on the nearest foe within 14 blocks and bite it together for about a heart and a half (a quarter of a heart each). They never attack you or your allies. After a minute (or if you die, leave, or cross to another world) they fly back into the jar.
Recall the Bats. They return to the jar at once.
Tabletop made game: "one hour" became one minute; controlled bats became a fixed bite so they cannot be exploited.
item.nusmp.jar_of_bats.desc: Open the jar and six bats swarm out, answering you: they fall on the nearest foe for a minute, then fly back in.
item.nusmp.simple_blue_runechalk.card:
Normal Grade charm. Common wondrous item. A short stick of teal-blue chalk, its tip glowing cyan. You can draw up to 20 symbols with it; two come back at every dawn.
Square: Alarm. A rune on the ground: for three minutes, the first time a foe comes within six blocks of it the rune flares, wakes you with a message and makes the intruder glow. At most two at a time.
Circle: Purify Food and Drink. Hunger, poison, nausea and magicule poison are lifted from you and your friends within five blocks, and spoiled food in your pack is made good (poisonous potatoes become potatoes, rotten flesh becomes raw beef, spider eyes become bread; 16 at most).
Triangle: Mending. The damaged tool or weapon in your hands is repaired by a fifth of its life.
Cross: Lock. The door, gate, trapdoor or container you look at is shut and sealed for three minutes: no one but you can open it.
Tabletop made game: the intelligence requirement is dropped; the 20 ft cube of Alarm became six blocks; "instantly locks a mechanical lock" became a seal.
item.nusmp.simple_blue_runechalk.desc: Twenty chalk symbols (two return at dawn): Square sets an alarm, Circle purifies food and drink, Triangle mends what is in your hand, Cross locks a door or chest.
item.nusmp.dryads_wedding_band.card:
Unique Grade charm. This cursed ring once belonged to a dryad who was forsaken at the altar. It cannot be removed from whoever puts it on unless they die.
Curse. Once worn, it stays on: Curios is told not to let it be taken off while you live. If it is off all the same, vines drag at you (slowness and weakness) until you put it on again, die, or three game days pass.
Passive. Small plants grow on you in place of hair: +2 maximum health, Tensura's Poison Resistance, and under the open sky by day the sun feeds you (a little saturation and a little healing every few seconds). Fire hurts you 25% more.
Speak with Plants (once a game day). Crops, saplings and stems within five blocks grow at once (twelve at most), the vines hold every foe within four blocks (slowness for 5 seconds) and you regenerate for 6 seconds.
Tabletop made game: the "daily charge of speak with plants" is kept; the curse is kept; hair became health and sunlight feeding.
item.nusmp.dryads_wedding_band.desc: A cursed ring of twined vines that cannot be taken off until you die. Plants grow on you; the sun feeds you, fire burns you worse, and once a day you can speak with plants and they obey.
item.nusmp.weaversong.card:
Rare Grade charm. Requires attunement. A silken charm containing a song of farewell, left by the Weavers who departed Hallownest for their old home.
Passive. +0.5 Luck while it is worn.
Weaverlings. While it is attuned and worn, three Weaverlings (cave spiders that obey you) walk at your side and fight your foes. A Weaverling that falls reappears two seconds later, and any that wanders more than eight blocks from you is teleported to your feet. They never attack you or your allies.
Call the Weaverlings (30 s cooldown). All three are teleported to your feet at once (missing ones are made), and are quick and strong for 10 seconds.
Tabletop made game: "attune over a long rest" became attunement; "five feet" became eight blocks; "two rounds" became two seconds.
item.nusmp.weaversong.desc: A silken charm with a farewell song in it. Three Weaverlings walk at your side and fight for you; one that falls comes back two seconds later, and strays are called to your feet.
item.nusmp.coin_of_draconic_luck.card:
Special Grade charm. Uncommon wondrous item. A large round gold coin with an embossed grinning dragon head.
Dragon's Bargain (three uses a game day, 2 second cooldown). Flip the coin: HEADS gives you Luck II and Strength for 30 seconds (+2 on the next rolls of the card); TAILS gives you Bad Luck II and Weakness for 30 seconds (-2).
If you take three tails in a row on one game day, a d20 is rolled: on a 1 the coin cracks in two and loses all magic until three dawns have passed.
Tabletop made game: ability checks and attack rolls became Luck and Strength; "if you do not have a coin, roll a d4" is not needed (the coin flips itself); the permanent loss became a three-dawn crack.
item.nusmp.coin_of_draconic_luck.desc: Flip the dragon's coin three times a day: heads brings luck and strength for half a minute, tails the opposite. Three tails in a row can crack the coin.
item.nusmp.alabaster_white_runechalk.car:
Rare Grade charm. A short, slightly rough stick of bright white chalk, a soft pale-blue glow behind it. You can draw up to 20 symbols with it (two come back at every dawn). Only one of the circle and the glyph can be active at a time.
Square: Stabilize. A friend (or you) at death's door is pulled back to at least four hearts, regenerates for 8 seconds and is cleansed of poison and wither. It does not affect the undead or constructs (golems).
Circle. A chalk circle three blocks wide on the ground for a minute: you and your friends who stand in it are Lucky and Hasty (the 1d4 bonus to one check).
Triangle: Sacred Glyph. A glyph on the ground for a minute: every second, undead creatures standing on it take 1d8+2 holy damage.
Cross: Erase. The written book in your hand becomes a blank book, or the filled map an empty map.
Tabletop made game: Dexterity saves of the undead became the damage each second; "ability check bonus" became Luck and Haste.
item.nusmp.alabaster_white_runechalk.des: Twenty chalk symbols (two return at dawn): Square pulls a friend back from death's door, Circle blesses those who stand in it, Triangle burns the undead, Cross wipes a book or map clean.
item.nusmp.strange_idol.card:
Rare Grade charm. A golden seated cat on a golden plinth, with glowing green eyes, a green crown and a stitched scar down its chest.
Passive. +0.5 Luck while it is worn.
Re-roll Fate (once a game day). Roll twice and take the higher: a random boon (Luck, Strength, Resistance, Speed, Haste or Regeneration) for 5 minutes, at a level of one to four (level III at most for Strength, Resistance and Regeneration). Each time, someone else near you (a random foe within 16 blocks) has disadvantage: Bad Luck II, Weakness, Slowness and a glow for 30 seconds (10 seconds if a player).
Tabletop made game: the re-rolled die became the better of two rolls for the level of a boon; "disadvantage on the next roll" became Bad Luck; the card's cut-off text is read as the original sentence.
item.nusmp.strange_idol.desc: A golden cat with a stitched green scar. Once a day it re-rolls fate in your favour, keeping the better of two rolls, and someone near you rolls with disadvantage.
item.nusmp.wallet_of_the_slayer.card:
Legend Grade charm. Can be a Djinn's Metal Vessel. A small item, easy to conceal, imbued with a dark magic that awards its holder with coin as reward for the taking of a life. The forces behind the magic are widely unknown.
Passive. Whenever your own hand kills a creature, the purse pays: Challenge Rating (its maximum health / 15, at least a quarter) times 2d6 gold pieces, at least 1, at most 600 per kill, up to a million in the purse. Players, summons, pets and villagers pay nothing. (The kill must be yours: the blow or spell that kills it.)
Count Coin (1 second cooldown). Pays the purse out in Tensura's coins (a gold coin is 100 gp, a silver coin 1 gp; gold nuggets if Tensura's coins are absent), 64 of each at most per use.
Blood Tithe (1 minute cooldown, 300 gp). The wallet drinks 300 gp from the purse and closes your wounds: heals 12 hit points and gives a shield of absorption.
Tabletop made game: gold pieces became Tensura's money; "the damage that kills" is the kill itself.
item.nusmp.wallet_of_the_slayer.desc: A singed wallet that pays coin for every life your own hand takes: its challenge times 2d6 gold. Count the coin out, or tithe it for healing.
item.nusmp.arcanists_notebook.card:
Common grade charm (Curios charm slot). Consult it: hold the use button for three seconds, then let go (or hold the worn-relic key). The card's "spend 1 minute and gain 1d4-1 to your Arcana check" has no ability checks to roll in the game, so the d4-1 (0 to 3) is rolled for the pages you read and decides how much the notebook had to say: it lasts two minutes plus one for every point (two to five minutes). Arcanist: Tensura's Magic Sense is lent to you for the study; from 2 pages on you also get Magicule Regeneration. Cooldown six minutes, longer than the longest study, so the bonus is never permanent.
Tabletop rules became: the Arcana check bonus -> Magic Sense and magicule regeneration for the study.
item.nusmp.arcanists_notebook.desc: Notes of a long-dead arcanist. Consult it (hold use) and its pages of 0 to 3 steady your sense of magic for two to five minutes.
item.nusmp.botanists_notebook.card:
Common grade charm (Curios charm slot). Consult it: hold the use button for three seconds, then let go (or hold the worn-relic key). The card's "spend 1 minute and gain 1d4-1 to your Nature check" has no ability checks to roll in the game, so the d4-1 (0 to 3) is rolled for the pages you read and decides how much the notebook had to say: it lasts two minutes plus one for every point (two to five minutes). Botanist: Poison Resistance is lent to you for the study, and from 1 page on you gain Luck (1 page Luck I, 2 pages Luck II, 3 pages Luck III); from 2 pages you forage a little food. Cooldown six minutes, longer than the longest study, so the bonus is never permanent.
Tabletop rules became: the Nature check bonus -> Luck and poison resistance (and a little food).
item.nusmp.botanists_notebook.desc: Notes of a long-dead botanist. Consult it (hold use) and you know which plants help and which kill: Luck and poison resistance for two to five minutes.
item.nusmp.historians_notebook.card:
Common grade charm (Curios charm slot). Consult it: hold the use button for three seconds, then let go (or hold the worn-relic key). The card's "spend 1 minute and gain 1d4-1 to your History check" has no ability checks to roll in the game, so the d4-1 (0 to 3) is rolled for the pages you read and decides how much the notebook had to say: it lasts two minutes plus one for every point (two to five minutes). Historian: you gain experience (5, +5 per page) and Tensura's Analytical Appraisal is lent to you for the study. Cooldown six minutes, longer than the longest study, so the bonus is never permanent.
Tabletop rules became: the History check bonus -> experience and Analytical Appraisal.
item.nusmp.historians_notebook.desc: Notes of a long-dead historian. Consult it (hold use) for a little experience and a sharper eye for what things are.
item.nusmp.physicians_notebook.card:
Common grade charm (Curios charm slot). Consult it: hold the use button for three seconds, then let go (or hold the worn-relic key). The card's "spend 1 minute and gain 1d4-1 to your Medicine check" has no ability checks to roll in the game, so the d4-1 (0 to 3) is rolled for the pages you read and decides how much the notebook had to say: it lasts two minutes plus one for every point (two to five minutes). Physician: you are healed (4 health points, +2 per page), gain Regeneration (stronger from 2 pages) and are cured of poison. Cooldown six minutes, longer than the longest study, so the bonus is never permanent.
Tabletop rules became: the Medicine check bonus -> healing, regeneration and a cure for poison.
item.nusmp.physicians_notebook.desc: Notes of a long-dead physician. Consult it (hold use) to dress your wounds: a quick mend, regeneration and no poison.
item.nusmp.theologians_notebook.card:
Common grade charm (Curios charm slot). Consult it: hold the use button for three seconds, then let go (or hold the worn-relic key). The card's "spend 1 minute and gain 1d4-1 to your Religion check" has no ability checks to roll in the game, so the d4-1 (0 to 3) is rolled for the pages you read and decides how much the notebook had to say: it lasts two minutes plus one for every point (two to five minutes). Theologian: you gain absorption hearts (2 health points, +2 per page) for a minute, Holy Attack Resistance is lent to you for the study and from 2 pages you also gain Resistance. Cooldown six minutes, longer than the longest study, so the bonus is never permanent.
Tabletop rules became: the Religion check bonus -> absorption and holy resistance.
item.nusmp.theologians_notebook.desc: Notes of a long-dead theologian. Consult it (hold use) for a remembered rite: a ward of absorption and resistance to holy harm.
item.nusmp.fast_travel_beads.card:
Rare grade charm.
The chain holds 3d10 beads (3 to 30), rolled the first time it is used. Break a Bead: breaks one bead to carry you, and up to six companions, to the destination chosen on the chain, on THIS plane (the Overworld, the Nether or the End; not the Dungeon). Companions are players within six blocks who are crouching (their consent), your tamed animals and your relic summons; each arrives on safe ground around the destination. Choose Destination (sneak and use): cycles your bed, the place you last fell, your saved marks, and a last slot that saves the place you stand on. Remember This Place (key, or use while the last slot is chosen): saves where you stand as a mark (six at most; a mark within eight blocks is replaced, else the oldest goes). If there is no safe ground at the destination, nothing is spent.
Tabletop rules became: "a place the user has been to before, known very well" -> a place you saved yourself, your bed or your grave; "6 other people" -> six who agree by crouching; "the DM's discretion" -> the safe-landing rule.
item.nusmp.fast_travel_beads.desc: A cord of starry beads, three to thirty of them. Break one to carry yourself and up to six crouching companions to a place of this world you have saved, your bed, or where you last fell.
item.nusmp.madama_cupcake.card:
Rare grade charm, one use. Eat it (use): it feeds you for three Minecraft days. While it lasts your hunger never falls below 17 of 20, so you never starve, yet you never feel bloated: you can still eat anything. Hunger (the effect) is cleared while it lasts. It is used up, and you cannot eat a second one while the first still feeds you.
Tabletop rules became: "sustains a medium creature for 3 days" -> 72000 ticks of a hunger floor; "can still eat while affected" -> the floor is 17, not 20.
item.nusmp.madama_cupcake.desc: A cupcake swirled with lavender frosting. Eat it and you will not go hungry for three days, yet you never feel bloated and can still eat. It is used up.
item.nusmp.bags_of_transferrence.card:
Legend grade charm, a Djinn vessel. Two burlap bags of two rows each, always together.
Open the Near Bag (use): the bag you carry. Open the Far Bag (key): the other bag. Speak the Command Words (sneak and use): the contents of the two bags trade places, whatever the distance. Link a Companion (key): the nearest crouching player within eight blocks holds the other bag; they reach the Far Bag from anywhere with the command /pouch far <your name> and can look in while you do. Using the link with no one beside you ends it. A bag takes anything except another pouch or storage garment, so nothing nests. The contents live in the world, not in the item: they stay if the item is lost, and travel with it if it changes hands.
Tabletop rules became: "a pair of bags, each the size of a pouch" -> two rows each; "a creature that knows the command words" -> the one who holds the relic; "no range limit, same plane" -> no limit at all; "cannot be located by magic" -> the contents are not carried in the item (a note only).
item.nusmp.bags_of_transferrence.desc: Two burlap bags that are one: a near bag and a far bag of two rows each. Speak the words and what is in one trades places with what is in the other, at any distance; link a friend and they reach the far bag with /pouch.
item.nusmp.lifes_emergency.card:
Unique grade charm. Requires attunement.
It draws life from the air: at each dawn it absorbs 10 points of stored life, up to 50 (the card's table: Uncommon 10, Rare 30, Very rare 50, Very rare 70, Legendary 90; this one is Very rare). While you wear it you are hardier (+2 maximum health). When a blow would kill you, the whole store floods back as health (0.4 health per stored point: 50 stored is a full 20-point bar, never above your maximum), you are cured of every effect and put out, and the cycle starts again from nothing. The void and commands that kill outright are not caught. Read the Cuff (use) shows what it holds.
Tabletop rules became: "falls below 0 hit points" -> a killing blow; "hit points" -> 0.4 health points each; "each new dawn" -> each Minecraft day.
item.nusmp.lifes_emergency.desc: A cuff that draws life from the air: ten points each dawn, up to fifty. Worn, you feel hardier; fall at death's door and the whole store floods back into you.
item.nusmp.bag_of_realistic_capacity.car:
Rare grade charm.
A small fist-sized pouch that fits exactly as much as it looks able to: two rows of nine slots, no more. Open the Pouch (use). Gather Loose Items (sneak and use): the pouch pulls in loose items within six blocks, twelve stacks at most. It takes anything except another pouch or storage garment. The contents live in the world, not in the item.
The card is a one-line joke (and only partly visible); the capacity and the gathering are the remainder invented for the game.
item.nusmp.bag_of_realistic_capacity.des: A fist-sized pouch that holds exactly as much as it looks like it can: two rows. Sneak and use to pull in the loose items around you.
item.nusmp.plastic_sheriff_badge.card:
Rare grade charm.
Worn: raiders (illagers, ravagers, witches) who would turn on you make the card's Bluff check once: a d20 + 3 against their resolve (10, up to 18 for the biggest creatures). If they believe it they leave you alone for ten seconds. Halt! In the Name of the Law (use): every foe within ten blocks makes the same check; those who believe lose their target, are afraid (Tensura fear) and slowed. The badge gives no discounts and no trade prices: "this coupon does not actually qualify for any discounts". Cooldown thirty seconds.
Tabletop rules became: "+3 to Bluff checks when impersonating a person of authority" -> a d20 + 3 contest against each target's resolve; the 500 gp coupon -> nothing.
item.nusmp.plastic_sheriff_badge.desc: A toy star that says SHERIFF. Raiders sometimes believe it and look away; call a halt and every foe near you tests your bluff.
item.nusmp.urn_of_black_pudding.card:
Unique grade charm, one use.
Throw the Urn (use): it flies up to 12 blocks and shatters on the first foe in your line of sight (or where you look). On a hit the target takes 1d8 x 1.5 acid-like damage (a player at most 30% of their health), is afflicted with Tensura Corrosion, and every nonmagical armour piece it wears (no enchantments, not a relic) loses 15% of its durability; a piece eaten through is gone. A small black pudding (6 health) is freed to fight for you for one minute. The urn is used up.
Tabletop rules became: "20 feet" -> 12 blocks; "ranged attack with an improvised weapon" -> aiming (a 20-degree cone); "permanent cumulative -1 AC" -> permanent cumulative durability loss; "5 hp" -> 6 health.
item.nusmp.urn_of_black_pudding.desc: A two-handled urn with a small black pudding inside. Throw it: acid for the target, its plain armour eaten away, and a small pudding fights for you. It shatters.
item.nusmp.crystal_dragon.card:
Rare grade charm, one use (the card is cut off at the bottom; the one-time use is the legible part).
Wake the Dragon (use, 8% of your magicules): an illusory dragon of shadow, huge and shadowy, rises over you for eight seconds. Its head follows where you look; once a second it breathes a cone of shadow (4 damage, fear on monsters). Players it breathes on lose at most 30% of their health to it in all. The statue is used up.
Tabletop rules became: the Illusory Dragon spell -> a dust-drawn dragon with a cone of shadow breath; the missing text -> invented as above.
item.nusmp.crystal_dragon.desc: A statue of a crystal dragon. Once, on your command, it unfolds into a huge shadowy dragon that follows your gaze and breathes shadow for eight seconds.
item.nusmp.shared_pouches_of_transfer.ca:
Rare grade charm.
A pair of pouches on one pocket dimension, three rows each side (a small backpack). Open the Pouches (use). Link a Companion (sneak and use, with a friend crouching within eight blocks): they reach the same items from anywhere with /pouch open <your name>, even while you look inside; using the link with no one beside you ends it. It takes anything except another pouch or storage garment. The contents live in the world, not in the item.
Tabletop rules became: "two creatures owning the two pouches" -> you and your linked companion (relics are one of a kind, so there is one item, and the second pouch is the link); "cannot be located by magic" -> not carried in the item (a note only).
item.nusmp.shared_pouches_of_transfer.de: A pair of sleepy green pouches on one pocket dimension, three rows deep. Link a friend (you both crouch) and you each reach the same items, from anywhere.
Rare grade charm.
Twenty enchanted sweets in a bag. Eat a Sweet (use): one sweet, and a roll on the wild magic table (a d20): glow, feather fall, high jump, a short float, healing, speed, queasiness, invisibility, fire ward, a little experience, a short hop, a sugary sneeze that shoves foes away, syrupy slowness, night sight, regeneration, an absorbing shell, haste, a shove forward, luck, or two more rolls. Most are kind and a few are not. The bag stays when it is empty. Cooldown three seconds.
Tabletop rules became: "the wild magic table" -> the d20 table above.
Twenty enchanted sweets in a twine-tied bag. Eat one and roll on the wild magic table: most are kind, some are not.
item.nusmp.the_devils_due.card:
Rare grade charm, one use.
Pay the Devil (use): the coin erupts in hellfire and a horned devil (Tensura's lesser daemon; a vex if Tensura is absent) steps out to fight at your side. It stays for five minutes (the most any relic ally may stay) or until it is slain, then returns to the Nine Hells. The coin is irrevocably destroyed. At most six relic allies at once.
Tabletop rules became: "up to an hour" -> five minutes; "hit points reduced to 0" -> it dies.
item.nusmp.the_devils_due.desc: A really bad penny, rusted and warm. Pay it with a thought: hellfire, and a horned devil fights at your side for five minutes. The coin is destroyed.
item.nusmp.fury_of_the_fallen.card:
Rare grade charm. Requires attunement.
When your health falls below 20% you light up with a red glow (dust and sparks around you), and every weapon attack you land deals double damage: melee blows and the arrows and bolts you loose. Magic and explosions are not weapon attacks. It ends when you heal above the line.
Tabletop rules became: "emitting dim light in a 5ft cube" -> a red glow of particles; "weapon attacks deal double damage" -> x2 on melee and projectiles.
item.nusmp.fury_of_the_fallen.desc: A dark badge with two slit eyes. When you fall under a fifth of your health you glow red, and every weapon blow you land does double damage.
item.nusmp.bag_of_holding.desc: A satchel far bigger on the inside: a chest of fifty-four slots that goes with you. No bag fits inside another.
item.nusmp.bag_of_holding.card: Wondrous item, uncommon. A bag with an interior far bigger than its outside. Right-click (or the Use Worn Relic key) opens it as a chest of 54 slots that goes with the bag: its contents are kept on the item itself, so it can be carried, dropped and found again. No bag may go inside another bag (tabletop: an extradimensional space inside another tears both and opens a gate to the Astral Plane; here the bag simply refuses it). Replaced rules: the 500-pound and 64-cubic-foot limit and 'overloaded, pierced or torn' ruptures are the fixed 54 slots; 'retrieving an item needs an action' is opening the bag; the 15-pound weight is not used; breathing creatures inside are not a thing (see the Bag of Kittens for a bag with creatures).
item.nusmp.bag_of_devouring.desc: The mouth of a vast creature. It eats food and plants put in it (and feeds you magicules for them), spits the rest out each day, and can gulp a small foe after three telegraphed seconds.
item.nusmp.bag_of_devouring.card: Wondrous item, very rare. The mouth of a gigantic extradimensional creature, disguised as a bag. Opens as a chest of 27 slots, but it eats: animal and vegetable matter (food, plants, anything a composter takes) put in is devoured and lost; each devoured item feeds you 0.25% of your maximum magicules (Tensura magicules), up to 30 items a day. Once each day, the first time it is opened, it swallows what else is inside and spits it all out at your feet (the 'spits them out into another plane' of the card). No bag goes inside it. Reach In (sneak and use, existence 2%, 1 min cooldown): the nearest small foe in front of you (width 1.4, height 2.5, up to 80 health) is pulled in with a 50% chance, less for a foe with knockback resistance (the Strength check). A pulled-in foe is pinned and glowing for three seconds (players are only slowed), then devoured for 40% of its maximum health (8 to 60), never past 45% of a player's health. Replaced rules: 'Strength DC 15 to escape' and 'DC 20 to pull out' are knockback resistance and the three-second warning; 'starts its turn inside and is destroyed' is the gulp, which does not kill outright; 'a cubic foot' is the 27 slots.
item.nusmp.bag_of_colding.desc: A cold larder for food, and a snack from it on the move. Stuffed with a foe, it chills it to the bone. Frost bites you less while you carry it.
item.nusmp.bag_of_colding.card: Wondrous item, rare. A Bag of Holding of 54 slots, but it is a cold larder: it takes only food. Carrying it cuts freezing damage by 30%. Cold Snack (with the Use Worn Relic key): eats one food item from the larder as you walk, fresh and chilled: it feeds half again as much and none of its bad side effects apply. Stuff the Bag (sneak and use, 3% mana, 30 s cooldown): the nearest small foe in front of you is pinned inside for three seconds. At each of three pulses (the 'end of each minute') it rolls a save against the bag (55% to fail, less with knockback resistance); a failed one deals 4 cold damage and frostbite and chills it (Tensura). A foe that fails twice of three gains the card's level of exhaustion: Mining Fatigue, Weakness and Hunger. Players are only slowed. Replaced rules: 40 degrees Fahrenheit is the freezing-damage cut and food only; 'DC 12 Constitution saves each minute' are the three pulses; 'exhaustion' is the three effects.
item.nusmp.bag_of_golding.desc: A tiny pouch for metal bars, nuggets and coins. Iron nuggets and copper left a day inside come out gilded as gold nuggets. A little luck clings to it.
item.nusmp.bag_of_golding.card: Wondrous item, rare. A Bag of Holding that holds only one pound: a single row of 9 slots, for metal bars, nuggets and coins. Metal left a day inside is gilded: iron nuggets become gold nuggets and copper ingots become three gold nuggets each, at most 64 items a day, checked when the bag is opened. Carrying it gives +0.5 luck. Replaced rules: 'gilded for 24 hours, then clear wax' is the one-day wait; the gold stays gold (the card's wax is dropped so a day's patience is the whole price).
item.nusmp.bag_of_molding.desc: A damp bag for plant matter that rots it down to bone meal in a day. Stuffed with a foe, it poisons it. You are used to the stench: poison resistance while carried.
item.nusmp.bag_of_molding.card: Wondrous item, rare. A damp Bag of Holding of 54 slots that takes only plant matter (anything a composter takes) and rots it: a day inside turns it to bone meal, one for every 5 composter levels, at most 64 items a day, checked when the bag is opened. Carrying it gives Tensura's poison resistance. Stuff the Bag (sneak and use, 3% mana, 30 s cooldown): the nearest small foe in front of you is pinned inside for three seconds. At each of three pulses it rolls a save against the bag (55% to fail, less with knockback resistance); a failed one deals 4 poison damage and Poison. A foe that fails twice of three is left poisoned: a longer Poison, Weakness and Nausea. Players are only slowed. Replaced rules: 'rot and decay' is the composting; the Constitution saves and 'poisoned for 1 hour' are the pulses and the long Poison/Weakness.
item.nusmp.bag_of_scolding.desc: A bag that cannot stand mess: it sorts what is in it every time it opens. Stuffed with a foe, it lectures it: it takes damage, fear and a weak arm.
item.nusmp.bag_of_scolding.card: Wondrous item, rare. A Bag of Holding of 54 slots that cannot stand a mess: it sorts its contents by name and merges stacks every time it is opened. Stuff the Bag (sneak and use, 3% mana, 30 s cooldown): the nearest small foe in front of you is pinned inside for three seconds while the bag lectures it. At each of three pulses it rolls a save against the bag (55% to fail, less with knockback resistance); a failed one deals 4 psychic damage, Tensura fear, and a weak arm (Weakness II for five seconds: the 'disadvantage on its next attack'). Players are only slowed. Replaced rules: the Wisdom saves each minute are the pulses; 'disadvantage' is Weakness.
item.nusmp.bag_of_unfolding.desc: A bag that unties things. It shakes webs and locks off you and unlatches the iron door, trapdoor or gate you point it at, eight times a day.
item.nusmp.bag_of_unfolding.card: Wondrous item, rare. A Bag of Holding of 54 slots that unties things. Unfold (sneak and use, eight uses a day, 1 s cooldown): shakes loose whatever holds you (Tensura webs, earth locks, a crushing slowness) and unlatches the iron door, trapdoor or fence gate you point it at (within six blocks; never in the Dungeon). Replaced rules: 'items left inside for 24 hours become unlocked' are the eight daily unlatchings; 'only one lock of several' is one door per use; 'arcane lock suppressed' is not used (no spell locks exist here).
item.nusmp.old_masters_spellbook.desc: Centuries of margins and smudges: spells come cheaper and abilities are learned faster, elemental damage glances off, and twice a day you find the shortcut in the old notes.
item.nusmp.old_masters_spellbook.card: Wondrous item, very rare. Centuries of margins and smudges: it does not wear out and elemental damage glances off it (fire, freezing and lightning damage cut by a quarter, explosions by 15%). Arcane focus: +8% maximum magicules, spells cost 10% less (Tensura's magic cost multiplier), abilities are learned and mastered 50% faster (Tensura's learning and mastery gain), and the old spell traces lend you Magic Sense while it is carried. Shortcut to Mastery (twice a day, 20 s cooldown): you find the shortcut in the old notes. For five minutes you have Tensura's Inspiration and Magic Aura, Haste, and Magic Sense. Replaced rules: copying a spell for half the cost and time is half the time and a tenth less cost on every spell and a faster learning of abilities; 'once for each spell' is twice a day; the Arcana check is dropped.
item.nusmp.tiny_orbit.desc: A thin silver chain circlet with a small illusory moon that orbits your head, and lights the dark a little for you.
item.nusmp.tiny_orbit.card: Wondrous item, uncommon. A very thin sterling silver chain circlet. A small illusory moon orbits your head while it is worn, visible to everyone. In the dark (light level under 4) it lights your way with a gentle night vision. Replaced rules: the card is pure flavour; the moon's glow became a little night vision.
item.nusmp.the_lovers_divide.desc: Bangles that join two hearts: for five minutes every blow either of you takes is split between you. The friend must be sneaking to agree, or be your own pet.
item.nusmp.the_lovers_divide.card: Wondrous item, rare. A pair of bangles joined by chains: they share all damage between the two who wear them. Join Hearts (use, 5 s cooldown): links you to the nearest friend within eight blocks who is sneaking (their consent) or to your own tamed pet. For five minutes, while you wear the bangles and both of you are within 32 blocks and in the same world, half of every blow either of you takes goes to the other (never taking the other's last health point; the void and /kill are not shared). A new link replaces the old one. Sever the Chains (sneak-use) ends it. Replaced rules: 'the two that wear them' is the wearer and a consenting friend or pet (there is only one copy of the relic); 'all damage' is half of each blow, so the sum is shared.
item.nusmp.coin_of_fortune.desc: Gold face for fortune, dark face for doom. Flip it three times a day: even is a blessing on your next blow dealt or taken and luck for five minutes, odd is the curse.
item.nusmp.coin_of_fortune.card: Wondrous item, uncommon. A golden face (Lady Luck) on one side, a dark face (Lady Doom) on the other. Flip the Coin (3 charges a day, back at dawn, 2 s cooldown): rolls a d20. Even is the gold face: good fortune, and your next blow dealt does half as much again (x1.5), or your next blow taken is cut to 70%, whichever comes first, plus Luck II for five minutes. Odd is the dark face: misfortune, the next blow you deal is x0.6 or the next you take x1.3, plus Bad Luck II for five minutes. The fortune ends at the end of the day. Replaced rules: 'advantage or disadvantage on the next ability check, attack or saving throw' is the blow dealt, the blow taken and luck.
item.nusmp.defenders_dial.desc: A dial of flame, snowflake and bolt. Turn it three times a day: each turn cuts one kind of damage by 60% for five minutes, in that order, then starts over.
item.nusmp.defenders_dial.card: Wondrous item (accessory), rare. A belt buckle with a dial showing a flame, a snowflake and a bolt. Turn the Dial (3 uses a day, back at dawn): sets the dial to the next picture, in order fire, freezing, lightning, and starts over. For five minutes damage of that kind is cut by 60% (Minecraft's fire, freezing and lightning damage tags). Turning to fire also puts you out. Replaced rules: 'resistance' is a 60% cut; 'three times per day' is the use counter.
item.nusmp.elephant_of_the_room.desc: Say your deepest secret out loud (sneak and use it) and it swells to fill the room: foes are shoved aside, wedged against the walls and slowed for half a minute. Only once, for ever.
item.nusmp.elephant_of_the_room.card: Wondrous item, rare. A little black wooden elephant. Fill the Room (sneak and use, once in the life of the figurine): you say your deepest secret out loud and the elephant swells to fill the room, a circle as wide as the room is open (5 to 12 blocks; the average distance to the walls around you). Foes inside are shoved aside as it swells, then for thirty seconds squeezing past it is difficult terrain (Slowness III), and a foe that is pressed against a wall is held: a mob gets Slowness VII, Weakness and Tensura's movement interference; a player only Slowness IV. You gain four hearts of protection (absorption) for the time. After thirty seconds it deflates; the figurine is then spent for good (An elephant never forgets). Replaced rules: 'inflates 20 feet a round', 'strength save of 18', 'AC 18 and 200 hit points' and '12 hours' are the shove, the wall check and the thirty seconds; 'once in your lifetime' is kept.
item.nusmp.bag_of_kittens.desc: A kitten paradise of a thousand kittens. Pick one to take with you (eight at most), pop one back in by sneaking, or turn the bag inside out for a flood of kittens that slows and blinds foes and cheers friends.
item.nusmp.bag_of_kittens.card: Wondrous item, very rare. A kitten paradise: the interior holds a thousand kittens, and keeps them young. It holds only kittens (it has no chest). Pick a Kitten (2 s cooldown): takes one kitten out as a tamed kitten that follows you (you may have eight cats in your care at once). Place a Kitten (sneak-use): a kitten of yours within four blocks hops back into the bag. Feline Flood (existence 2%, 90 s cooldown): turns the bag inside out. A flood of kittens pours out around you for 3d6 seconds (3 to 12): the circle starts four blocks wide and grows each second, up to nine blocks with a full bag (smaller with fewer kittens). Foes in it are slowed (difficult terrain) and mobs are blinded (heavily obscured); you and your friends and pets are healed gently (purring). Three tame kittens show it. Replaced rules: 'indestructible' is kept; 'an action' is the use; '30 feet, +10 feet a turn, 3d6 turns' is the radius table and the seconds.
item.nusmp.the_pocket_campsite.desc: Point the pouch and press the rune: a large tent with a bed, two small tents and a campfire with seats appear, with a tiny hut over them. Sneak and press it again to pack it all away.
item.nusmp.the_pocket_campsite.card: Wondrous item, rare. A small pouch with a rune on the back. Pitch the Camp (right-click, 10 s cooldown): point the pouch and press the rune. A large tent (red wool) with a bed, two small tents (yellow and blue wool) and a campfire with four slab seats appear in front of you, about a hundred blocks of wool, slabs, a fire and a bed, on flat open ground (about eleven blocks ahead; it is refused when there is no room, and in the Dungeon). Tiny Hut: for ten minutes, within seven blocks of the fire, everyone resting mends (Regeneration and Saturation) and hostile mobs are turned away. Pack Up (sneak and use): the whole camp folds back into the pouch (only the blocks it placed, if they are still there). Replaced rules: the 'Tiny Hut' spell is the ring above; the camp is real blocks, so packing it up removes them; the hut ends when the ten minutes are up and is forgotten if the server restarts (the tents stay until packed).
item.nusmp.mirror_of_spell_reflection.de: Raise the mirror (three times a day, for a little mana) and the next spell that strikes you within five seconds is thrown back at its caster.
item.nusmp.mirror_of_spell_reflection.ca: Wondrous item, very rare. An ornate hand mirror of polished silver glass. Raise the Mirror (3 uses a day, 2% mana, 15 s cooldown): for five seconds you hold the mirror up, with a Tensura magic barrier. The next spell that strikes you in that time (magic damage from a caster: Minecraft magic or any Tensura non-physical damage) is cancelled and thrown back at the caster, for the same damage up to 30. Only one spell is caught per raising. Replaced rules: 'attack roll as a reaction' is the five-second window; 'each reflected spell uses a spell slot' is the mana; 'not above your highest spell level' is the damage cap of 30; three per day is the use counter.
item.nusmp.dragon_satchel.desc: Fill it (sneak and use) with two handfuls of ash, sand, grass or snow; in a day it is crystal powder. Throw a handful in a cone for fire, lightning, acid or cold damage. Twice empties it.
item.nusmp.dragon_satchel.card: Wondrous item, rare. A small satchel with a golden dragon head on the flap. Fill the Satchel (sneak and use): takes two handfuls from your pack of one material, ash (charcoal, coal, soul sand), sand (sand, red sand), grass (grass, fern, vines) or snow (snowballs, snow blocks); it must be empty. Over one Minecraft day the material turns to crystal powder. Throw Powder (1 s cooldown): throws one handful in a cone about five blocks long. Foes in the cone take 3d4 damage (halved for a foe that dodges, 40%) of the powder's kind: ash (red) is fire and sets them alight, sand (yellow) is lightning and slows, grass (green) is acid and poisons, snow (blue) is cold and slows and freezes. Throwing twice empties the satchel. Replaced rules: 'Dexterity save DC 15' is the 40% dodge; the 10 foot cone is five blocks; '24 hours' is one Minecraft day.
item.nusmp.spellbook_of_concentration.de: A red spellbook that glows softly and steadies the mind: more magicules and a firmer stance. Once a day it prepares the two spells on its marked page; once a day a short revision lends another page for five minutes.
item.nusmp.spellbook_of_concentration.ca:
Requires attunement (the card asks for a wizard; any attuned bearer may use it). Carried as a Charm.
Soft Light: the open book calms the mind. While attuned you gain +10% maximum magicules (Tensura) and 15% knockback resistance, so a blow does not break your focus.
Prepare Spells (once a Minecraft day, the long rest): the book has three pages of two spells each (Bolt and Ward: Magic Bullet and Magic Barrier; Mind and Sense: Thought Acceleration and Magic Sense; Insight and Aura: Analytical Appraisal and Magic Aura). The bookmark marks a page; Prepare lends you its two spells for a whole day. They are Tensura skills; a skill the world's list lacks is skipped, and if none can be lent a share of magicules flows back instead.
Turn the Page (sneak): moves the bookmark to the next page.
Revise (once a day, hold for five seconds, the short rest): lends the two spells on the page after the bookmark for five minutes, on top of what is prepared.
Tabletop became: "additional prepared spells equal to half your proficiency bonus" is two spells at a time; "replace prepared spells on a short rest" is the five-minute revision; spells of 5th level or lower is every page; "long rest" is a Minecraft day.
item.nusmp.fey_honey.desc: Silver honey in a jar. Drink it for twenty minutes of irresistible charm: Luck III, Hero of the Village and Thought Communication. When it wears off, fail the save and a wild magic surge bursts out of you.
item.nusmp.fey_honey.card:
Consumable, Rare. Silver honey with the consistency of mercury, sweet and intoxicating.
Drink it: for twenty minutes your force of personality is 21: Luck III, Hero of the Village, and Tensura's Thought Communication lent to you. Drinking it while it already works does nothing and the jar is kept.
When it wears off a Constitution save (DC 10, d20) is rolled: fail it and a wild magic surge erupts from you (the table of the Scroll of Unreadable Spells). A pool of magicules at 80% or more counts as being of the Fey and is spared automatically.
Tabletop became: "Charisma 21 for 1 hour" is Luck, Hero and a lent skill for twenty minutes (an hour is twenty minutes); "Fey creatures succeed automatically" is a full magicule pool.
item.nusmp.blood_chocolates.desc: Dark chocolate with a bitter, metallic centre. Heals ten health at once, but for seven minutes holy light hurts you twice as much.
item.nusmp.blood_chocolates.card:
Consumable, Uncommon. The sweet, syrupy filling of this dark chocolate has a metallic taste.
Eat it: you regain ten health at once and a little hunger, but for about seven minutes you take double damage from radiant, holy and sacred sources (including Holy Water).
Tabletop became: "vulnerability to radiant damage for 20 minutes" is double damage for seven minutes (a tabletop minute-count of twenty stretched to a third).
item.nusmp.ale_lemental.desc: A tankard of strange liquid. Pour it out and a water elemental of ale rises to fight at your side for half a minute.
item.nusmp.ale_lemental.card:
Consumable. An old tankard with strange liquid inside.
Pour it out: a water elemental made of ale (Tensura's Undine; a snow golem in plain Minecraft) rises, takes your side and fights for half a minute, then dissipates. It also puts out any fire on you. One use.
Tabletop became: "3 rounds" is thirty seconds (three rounds are too short to matter in real time); "acts as a water elemental" is the Undine.
item.nusmp.mug_of_the_boss.desc: "World's Best Boss." Once a day, chug it for a twenty-minute title (Boss, General, Lich, Chef or Wizard) and awe the creatures that see it. Sneak to change the title. You will sing in the bath and be hopeless at the helm.
item.nusmp.mug_of_the_boss.card:
Consumable (kept, not used up), Rare. A plain ceramic mug carved with odd runes that read "World's Best Boss".
Sneak while you drink to change the word (Boss, General, Lich, Chef, Wizard); the mug is kept. Otherwise, once every 24 hours (a Minecraft day), chug a full cup: the title takes hold for twenty minutes and the creatures that see the mug are moved. Boss: Hero of the Village, and hostile creatures within twelve blocks under sixty health stop hunting anyone for a minute. General: Strength I and Speed I, shared with your pets. Lich: undead within sixteen blocks stop hunting anyone for a minute, Night Vision, Poison Resistance lent. Chef: a full meal and Regeneration. Wizard: Sage and Magic Sense lent, a third of your magicules back.
The flaws: while a title lasts you sing in the water (notes and a banjo), you volunteer for everything (a little hunger drain) and you cannot steer (bad luck while riding a boat or a minecart).
Tabletop became: "advantage on charisma checks" is the awe above; "disadvantage operating a vehicle" is bad luck; "volunteering" is hunger; "wisdom save 15" is a health threshold.
item.nusmp.holy_water.desc: A flask of blessed water. Hurl it up to twelve blocks: eight radiant damage to fiends and the undead in a small splash, nothing to anyone else.
item.nusmp.holy_water.card:
Consumable. Improvised weapon (radiant): hurl it, or splash it on a creature close by.
Throw it: it flies up to twelve blocks along your look line and shatters on the first fiend or undead creature or block, splashing a two-block radius: eight radiant damage to fiends and the undead only (the undead tag, blazes, ghasts, withers, Tensura's daemons and undead). Everything else is untouched. A player made vulnerable by Blood Chocolates takes it doubled.
Tabletop became: "2d6 radiant, 5 ft splash or 20 ft throw" is 8 damage, a two-block splash and a twelve-block throw.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_unreadable_spells.d: Red letters no one can read. Read one aloud and roll the wild magic table: seven letters a day, back at dawn. No outcome can kill you.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_unreadable_spells.c:
Consumable, Rare. Written by a crazy mage, used by even crazier adventurers.
Read a letter aloud: roll one d100 on the Wild Magic Table (eighteen outcomes: glitter, levitation, mending, a ring of fire, feather fall, vanishing, swift feet, a misty step, swapping places with a foe, a stink cloud, a bolt of lightning, a flock of sheep, dread, a blinding flash, a magicule surge, a bloom of growth, a backfire and, rarely, a wish). Seven letters a day; they come back at dawn. The scroll is never used up. No outcome can kill you: backfire only stings when you have seven health or more, and creative or spectator players are never hit.
Tabletop became: the d100 table is a bounded Minecraft table; "charges fill every morning" is seven uses per Minecraft day.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_absorption.desc: Held in a hand, it draws in the next spell aimed only at you and cancels it. Read it afterwards to cast that spell back at a foe.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_absorption.card:
Consumable, Legendary. Valued by powerful archmages, cautious kings and paranoid warlords alike.
Hold the scroll in either hand: when a spell aimed at you from a creature (magic, an elemental bolt, a lance, a beam, a breath) would hit you, the damage is cancelled and the spell is drawn into the scroll, which now carries it (up to 24 damage). Read a charged scroll and the spell goes back out at the foe you are looking at (or the nearest within 24 blocks) with the damage and type it had; the scroll is used up. Read an empty scroll and it only reminds you how it works.
Tabletop became: "use your reaction" is simply holding it (no action needed); "a spell that targets only you, not an area" is any single-source magical hit; "becomes an ordinary spell scroll of that spell" is the charged scroll that casts it once.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_charm_parson_bargai: Scroll of Charm Parson (Bargain Bin Scrolls #1)
A misspelt Charm Person that works only on clergy. Cleric villagers, holy knights and creatures in holy gear nearby are charmed for five minutes.

Consumable (Bargain Bin Scroll #1). A spelling mistake means this spell, meant to coerce someone into believing you are their ally, now works only on members of the clergy.
Read it: cleric villagers, Tensura's holy knights and any creature in holy-engraved gear within sixteen blocks (twelve at most) are charmed for five minutes: they stop hunting you until you strike them. A creature of a hundred health or more shrugs it off. A charmed cleric villager leaves you Hero of the Village for twenty minutes. With no clergy about the scroll is kept.
Tabletop became: "DC 20 Wisdom save" is a health threshold; "charmed for 1 hour" is five minutes; clerics, paladins and priests are the clergy above.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_firball_bargain_bin: A misspelt Fireball: a swirling ball of pine needles that bursts for 12 piercing damage in a small radius. No fire.

Consumable (Bargain Bin Scroll #2). Presumably meant to be a fireball, this spelling error launches a swirling ball of pine needles.
Read it: the ball flies up to 28 blocks along your look line and bursts at the first creature or block, dealing 12 piercing damage to every foe within 3.5 blocks (half if the foe dodges: three in ten do). No fire, no block damage; the damage to players is capped as every relic's is.
Tabletop became: "8d6 piercing in a 20 ft sphere, DC 15 Dexterity save for half" is 12 damage in 3.5 blocks with a d20 DC 15 dodge.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_speak_with_rocks_ba: Scroll of Speak with Rocks (Bargain Bin Scrolls #3)
The rocks answer, and have nothing interesting to say, but they know where the nearby ores are.

Consumable (Bargain Bin Scroll #3). A spell that never made it out of beta testing: it works like speak with animals, but only on rocks. Early feedback: they never have anything interesting to say.
Read it: the rocks answer in chat (and do say nothing interesting), but they know where the ore is: every ore within ten blocks (24 at most) glimmers for a moment and the five nearest are named in chat with how far away they are.
Tabletop became: a joke spell with no mechanics became a short ore sense.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_summon_greater_crab: Scroll of Summon Greater Crab (Bargain Bin Scrolls #4)
A prototype summoning that was abandoned for a reason: a giant crab claws up in a marked ring and is hostile to everyone, you included. It dissolves after twenty seconds.

Consumable (Bargain Bin Scroll #4). A prototype summoning scroll abandoned after an increasing trend of pincer-related deaths.
Read it: a red ring is drawn on the ground six blocks ahead and shrinks for two and a half seconds; then a huge crab (Tensura's armoured beast, enlarged; the ravager in plain Minecraft) claws up. It is hostile to everyone, you included, hits for 5, and dissolves after twenty seconds. At most two per caster. Step out of the ring, or run.
Tabletop became: a 15 ft hulking crab hostile to all is a scaled-up armoured beast with a telegraph and a time limit.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_mace_hand_bargain_b: Scroll of Mace Hand (Bargain Bin Scrolls #5)
Your hand turns to solid iron for twenty minutes: with the main hand empty, every punch hits for 5 more.

Consumable (Bargain Bin Scroll #5). One simple quill stroke forgotten by the scribe has changed mage hand into something altogether different.
Read it: for twenty minutes your hand curls into a fist, swells and hardens into solid iron. With your main hand empty every blow deals 5 more damage.
Tabletop became: "1d6 + Strength bludgeoning for 1 hour" is +5 on a bare-fist hit for twenty minutes.
item.nusmp.scroll_of_facsimile_copy_barg: Scroll of Facsimile Copy (Bargain Bin Scrolls #6)
Hold a tool, weapon, armour piece, food or potion in your other hand and read it: a poorer copy appears in your pack and crumbles within minutes. Copies of copies are poorer still.

Consumable (Bargain Bin Scroll #6). Now discontinued for quality reasons, this spell lets you hold an object in one hand and summon a poorer copy.
Read it with the thing to copy in your other hand (a tool, weapon, armour piece, food or potion; no relics, no containers): a copy appears in your pack, one item, its enchantments gone, a damageable one with only half the durability the original had left. The copy crumbles to dust after ten minutes; a copy of a copy is a third as good and lasts five minutes; a third generation lasts two and a half; a fourth cannot be made.
Tabletop became: "an object no larger than 1 square foot" is the kinds of thing above; "half the quality, worse each time" is durability and a shrinking life.
item.nusmp.spotlight.card: While you hold it, you glow: the blade keeps you in the centre of attention (Glowing, which every creature can see). Once a day, right-click calls down a beam of bright light: for 20 seconds you have Night Vision and your next melee blow lands true (+50 percent damage, at most 6 extra, 3 against players). Tabletop "advantage on your next die roll" became that guaranteed stronger blow; the +1 became its base damage.
item.nusmp.spotlight.desc: A shortsword whose blade is a beam of stage light. You cannot help but be the centre of attention: it keeps you glowing. Once a day a beam finds you, you see in the dark and your next blow lands true.
item.nusmp.duality_blade.card: Needs attunement. Its blows carry necrotic and radiant harm. In dim light or darkness (light level 7 or less) the unseen blade adds 3.5 damage and withers the foe. Right-click toggles the Streamers of Light: you shine (Glowing and Night Vision), blows add 3.5 radiant damage (half as much again against the undead) and set the foe glowing; this negates the Blade of Darkness. In bright light with the streamers off, it adds a plain 2. Against players the bonus is capped at 2. The +3 attack roll became the extra damage.
item.nusmp.duality_blade.desc: A matte black shortsword that hides in the dark. In dim light it strikes with unseen, withering force; switch on its streamers of light and it shines, sets the foe aglow and burns the undead.
item.nusmp.frostfang.card: Needs attunement. Blows add 6 cold damage (3 against players), chill and slow the foe, and you resist cold and freezing. Right-click casts Cone of Cold: a 10-block cone of frost for 14 damage (45 percent cap on players), freezing and slowing everything in it; it costs 1 percent of your existence points and recharges in two minutes (the short rest). Sneak-click toggles Footfalls of Ice: still water under and around you freezes into frosted ice that melts again, and a chill trails your steps. The +3 attack bonus became the added damage; the spell save DC became the cone's guaranteed chill.
item.nusmp.frostfang.desc: A battleaxe with a horned, frost-rimed skull for a head. Every blow adds cold and chills the foe. Right-click casts a Cone of Cold (it costs existence points and needs a rest); sneak-click toggles Footfalls of Ice, which freeze water under your steps.
item.nusmp.soul_shatter_blade.card: Needs attunement. Cursed: a kill heals you by the harm the blow dealt (the surplus becomes temporary hearts, up to 8, for a minute) and gives you one soul fragment that stays with you through death and un-attuning. 5 fragments: Inflict Wounds (right-click, a necrotic touch for 14 within 4.5 blocks) with 2 charges a day. 10: a dark aura, every blow adds 3.5 necrotic damage and withers the foe. 15: 3 charges. 20: sneak-click Animate Dead (two skeleton servants for a minute, spends a charge) and Speak with Dead (the dead name every living thing within 24 blocks: Glowing, plus Magic Sense for 30 seconds). 25: the lich speaks through the blade now and then, and a plain golden apple can no longer lift the curse. 30: the lich's call: while you hold the blade you strike 2 harder and your maximum health is 2 hearts lower. An enchanted golden apple removes every fragment (greater restoration); a golden apple does while you are under 25 (remove curse). Charges return at dawn (the long rest).
item.nusmp.soul_shatter_blade.desc: A cursed lich's greatsword that drinks the dying: a kill heals you by the harm you dealt (the surplus becomes temporary hearts) and adds a soul fragment that stays with you. Fragments wake Inflict Wounds (5), a dark aura (10), a third charge (15), Animate Dead (20), the lich's voice (25) and its call (30). Golden apples cleanse.
item.nusmp.buster_sword.card: A two-handed slab: keep the off hand empty or each blow is a fifth weaker. It braces you against knockback. Right-click is Braver: leap high and land in a shockwave (9 damage in 4.5 blocks, knocks foes away; costs mana). Sneak-click is Cross-Slash: two cuts in front of you for 8 and a slow. The card has only its damage and two-handed rule; the two techniques are added after the sword's namesake, as the nearest fitting abilities.
item.nusmp.buster_sword.desc: A huge slab of steel with a red-wrapped grip and two materia holes. Hold it with both hands (an empty off hand): a full-strength blow is heavy. Braver leaps and lands in a shockwave; sneak-click for a Cross-Slash.
item.nusmp.dragon_tooth_blade_red.card: Two blows in a row on the same foe within three seconds make it burst into flame (7 extra damage, 3 against players, and it burns for 5 seconds). Right-click lights the fang for 10 seconds: every blow sets the foe alight. You take a quarter less fire damage and lend Flame Attack Resistance. The +2 became its base damage; the "same turn" became the three-second window. Searing Fang is added.
item.nusmp.dragon_tooth_blade_red.desc: A long, thin, strongly curved fang of a blade. Two blows in a row on the same foe make it burst into flame. Right-click lights the fang for ten seconds: every blow sets the foe alight. Fire hurts you less.
item.nusmp.corpse_eater.card: Needs attunement. Frenzy form: reach is 2 blocks longer (10 feet) and every blow adds 3.5 necrotic damage. Right-click: The Eye Opens, creatures in a 12-block cone who can see it must resist (about 40 percent for mobs, 30 for players, 75 or more for bosses) or be paralysed (3 seconds at most for players, 5 for mobs); a creature that resists is immune for 5 minutes (the card's hour). It costs 1 percent of your existence points and recharges in a minute. Sneak-click: Rending Bite, 8 necrotic damage and a festering wound to the foe in front of you, and you heal 3. Feeding Frenzy: whenever a living creature dies within 36 blocks (120 feet) you gain Haste, Speed (and Strength on the third) for 8 seconds and go hungry: the "immediate action" became the faster swings.
item.nusmp.corpse_eater.desc: A katana whose edge has split open around a staring eye. Frenzy form: two blocks more reach and a necrotic edge. The eye can hold those who see it (they may resist), a Rending Bite tears the foe and feeds you, and every death within thirty-six blocks sends sword and wielder into a Feeding Frenzy.
item.nusmp.random_axe_of_charity.card: A plain handaxe with a little luck (+1 Luck). Each non-player creature you kill with it drops 1 to 3 copper ingots (2d4 copper pieces, about one ingot to three pieces). Right-click throws it at the foe in front of you (12 blocks, 7 damage) and it is back in your hand at once.
item.nusmp.random_axe_of_charity.desc: A plain handaxe with a blood-red stain. Each creature it fells drops a few copper ingots. It brings a little luck, and you can throw it at a foe in sight without losing it.
item.nusmp.leviathan_axe.card: Needs attunement. The card is cut off after its header, so this kit is invented around its name. You resist cold and freezing and carry Cold Resistance. Blows add 3 cold damage and chill the foe. Right-click: Leviathan Throw, the axe flies 20 blocks in a straight line (stopped by walls) for 10 damage, chilling and nearly stopping everything it passes, and 0.7 seconds later it flies back along the line to your hand for 6 more, dragging the foes with it (costs mana). Sneak-click: Frost Awakening, for 12 seconds the runes burn: blows add 6 cold damage and freeze harder, and a freezing fog chills every foe within 4 blocks (costs 1 percent of your existence points).
item.nusmp.leviathan_axe.desc: A rune-carved frost axe. Right-click throws it down a line of twenty blocks, chilling everything it passes, and it flies back to your hand, dragging foes with it. Sneak-click awakens its runes: a freezing fog and colder blows for twelve seconds.
item.nusmp.shadow_burn.card: Needs attunement. You carry Shadow Motion. A foe standing in dim light burns: +2 damage and set alight. Right-click: Burning Hold, thrust the blade into the shadow of the foe in front of you (5.5 blocks, one that is much larger than you slips free): a failed save means 9 fire damage, burning and paralysis (the balance law's duration caps), a passed one half the fire (about 45 percent for mobs, 35 for players, 75 or more for bosses). It costs mana. Sneak-click: Shadow Stalk, twice a day (they return at dawn): you vanish into your shadow and rise behind the foe nearest your line of sight within 20 blocks, and your next blow lands true (+40 percent, at most 8).
item.nusmp.shadow_burn.desc: A heavy greatsword pulled from the heart of shade to serve the light, wrapped in shadow wisps. Foes standing in shadow burn. Burning Hold drives it into a foe's shadow (fire, and paralysis unless they resist); sneak-click for Shadow Stalk, twice a day: rise behind a foe within twenty blocks.
item.nusmp.hyperborean_crossbow.desc: A slim crossbow of the far north with a bowstring of blue light. Its bolts hit one point harder and slow what they strike. Sneak + use arms the next bolt to freeze the ground where it lands.
item.nusmp.hyperborean_crossbow.card: A real crossbow, drawn and loaded as any crossbow is; needs attunement. Its bolts deal 1 more damage, and a creature it hurts is slowed by half (Slowness III and Tensura's Frost) for 3 seconds, half that against a boss (a Constitution saving throw becomes that halving). It is a spellcasting focus: while you hold it your spells hit 10% harder. Held, it lends Cold Resistance and Freeze, and halves freezing damage. Flash Freeze: Surface (sneak + use, 3% mana, 5 s): the next bolt, within 30 seconds, freezes the ground where it lands: water in a 2.5 block radius turns to frosted ice, and for a minute (the card's 1 minute) the circle slows everything that crosses it (Slowness II and Frost), except you and your allies. Three patches per player at most, twelve in the world.
item.nusmp.druidic_blade.desc: A leaf-shaped blade handed down by the elven druids. Three times a day it calls grass and vines up round a point you look at and holds everything there in place.
item.nusmp.druidic_blade.card: Entangle (use, 3 a day, 5 s): grass and vines rise round the point you look at, up to 16 blocks away, and hold every foe within 5 blocks for 4 seconds (Slowness VII and Tensura's Earth Lock), half that against a boss. The card's 'once per short rest, no spell slot' becomes three uses a day and no mana. Held, it lends Poison Resistance.
item.nusmp.axe_of_the_exile.desc: A bone-hafted handaxe that you throw and that comes back to your hand. It carries the Exile's curse: near your bed or the world spawn it wears you out; far from home it lightens your step.
item.nusmp.axe_of_the_exile.card: Throw the Axe (use, 2.5 s): the axe flies up to 20 blocks along your line of sight, hits the nearest foe for 6 damage and is back in your hand at once (the card's Returning; the cooldown is its flight). Cursed, Exile: while you hold it (either hand) within 160 blocks of your bed (or the world spawn if you have none), your food bar drains twice as fast (the card's exhaustion), and it tells you why once. Far from home the curse turns: you walk 10% faster. The curse ends when you put the axe away. The card's 'cannot speak to loved ones' has no meaning here and is not played.
item.nusmp.astralaria.desc: A brass battleaxe filled with the night sky. Every blow adds radiant damage, you see through every illusion, and a cosmic trail follows the blade. Sneak + use scatters stars under your steps.
item.nusmp.astralaria.card: Needs attunement. Every blow adds 4.5 radiant damage (the card's 3d6 as a flat bonus) with a burst of stars. Held, it lends Eye of Truth and night vision (truesight), and anything invisible within 16 blocks is shown with a glow. Astral Sweep (use, 6% mana, 12 s): a burst of night sky round you deals 9 magic damage to every foe within 6 blocks and marks them glowing for 5 seconds. Cosmic Footprints (sneak + use): switches on or off a trail of stars under your steps. Every blow that lands leaves a trail of stars. The card's cut-off third text (an aura of fire) is not part of this weapon.
item.nusmp.null_blade.desc: A black greatsword with an eye in its cross. It frightens the weak, deals cold, eats maximum health and gives it to you as warding. After twenty lives it awakens. Anyone but its owner drops it.
item.nusmp.null_blade.card: Needs attunement; anyone but its attuned owner drops it and takes 3 cold damage (the card's 'forced to drop it, 1d6 cold'). Lesser creatures within 5 blocks flinch with Tensura's Fear. Each blow adds 3 cold damage and Frost, and takes up to 3 hearts of maximum health from the creature (a roll of d6 as half a heart per pip; at most 30% of a player, 8 health points, 2 minutes; at most half of a mob, 5 minutes), giving you temporary hit points equal to what it took, up to 10. When you shrug off a hostile spell the blade gains a charge (3 at most); Blindness / Deafness (use, 5 s) spends one: foes within 8 blocks are blinded and silenced for 5 seconds. The eye in the cross (automatic, every 10 s): a foe that strikes you from within 5 blocks is restrained (Slowness V and Frost, 2.5 s); if it strikes you again within 5 seconds it is frozen (Slowness VII and Frost for 5 s, Paralysis for 2.5 s); half that against a boss. Awakened after 20 kills with it: halves cold and necrotic damage; Armor of Agathys (sneak + use, once a day): 10 absorption for a minute, and whoever strikes you in melee takes 3 cold and Frost.
item.nusmp.viper_whip.desc: A whip of snakeskin that ends in a viper's head. It reaches further and poisons. Once a day the viper bites: for ten minutes you feel which way the bitten one lies.
item.nusmp.viper_whip.card: +1.5 blocks of reach. Each blow adds 2.5 poison damage and Poison for 5 seconds. Held, it lends Poison Resistance. Viper's Bite (use, once a day): the viper bites the foe you struck last (or the one you face within 6 blocks): for 10 minutes (the card's 12 hours) the action bar shows its direction and distance, alive, fallen or last known, up to 1000 blocks and across worlds.
item.nusmp.caesars_gladius.desc: A marbled gladius with a feathered guard. Once every five days it calls three gladiators for five minutes. Once in ten calls they remember the Republic, and turn on you.
item.nusmp.caesars_gladius.card: Call the Gladiators (use, 5% mana, every 5 days): three gladiators (Tensura lizardmen, or iron golems without Tensura) fight beside you for five minutes (the card's ten, the game's ally limit). One call in ten they remember the Republic: after 30 to 90 seconds, with a warning five seconds before, they turn into three hostile Gladiators of the Republic who hunt you for three minutes (the card's 'indefinitely') or until they fall.
item.nusmp.twin_swords_of_deflection.des: The right one of a matched pair of hooked blades. With the left one in your off hand both land with each blow; a tenth of blows are critical, and the wielder is quicker. Use to parry: missiles turn back on their sender.
item.nusmp.twin_swords_of_deflection.car:
Needs attunement (attuning one sword attunes both; the pair uses one of your three places). Pair: needs the other half. Hold one in the main hand and the other in the off hand: the off-hand sword adds a second blow of 60% of the first (own cooldown of 0.6 seconds), and the pair-only effects wake. One half alone keeps its abilities at a small penalty.
The pair strikes as one: the off-hand blade lands a second blow of 60% of the first, and one blow in ten is a critical (+50%, the card's 19 and 20). Dexterity +1 becomes +12% attack speed and +5% movement speed. Deflect (use, 2% mana, 6 s, shared by both swords): for 2 seconds missiles turn back on the one who sent them, melee blows lose 60% of their force and the attacker takes a 2.5 damage riposte. 4.4 damage each. The card is cut off after the Dexterity line; Deflect is added to fit its name.
item.nusmp.hunger.desc: A sentient greataxe with a mouth for a blade. It adds acid to every blow. Three times a day it devours a hit and gives you the blood as temporary health. If it goes hungry for three minutes it gnaws at you.
item.nusmp.hunger.card: A sentient greataxe. Each blow adds 4 acid damage (the card's 1d12) and Tensura's Corrosion. Held, it lends Danger Sense (its Wisdom +5). Devouring (use, 3 a day): for 20 seconds the next hit that draws blood gives you temporary hit points equal to the damage, up to 10 (6 against a player). Curse (the card is cut off after 'Every'): if it draws no blood for 3 minutes it gnaws at you, half a heart every 20 seconds, never below two hearts; any hit or kill feeds it.
item.nusmp.thornblight.desc: A thorn-hafted handaxe you can throw. Four times a day, thorns grow in the wound of the foe you struck last and fester. Its curse: every blow that lands costs you a point of health.
item.nusmp.thornblight.card: Throw the Axe (use, 2.5 s): the axe flies 18 blocks along your line of sight, hits the nearest foe for 7 damage and comes back. Spiteful Thorns (sneak + use, 4 a day, 3 s): thorns grow in the wound of the foe you struck within the last 10 seconds: Poison for 12 seconds (about 9 damage, never lethal) and Slowness. Curse: every blow that lands costs you 1 point of health, never the last two hearts. Milk ends the poison (the card's Remove Curse).

nusmp.skill.book_air.description: A grimoire of Air. Its pages are a bolt, a line, a field, a domain and a guard, all in the colour of the magic. Summon your grimoire, select a page, and press the skill key to cast.
nusmp.page.book_air.attribute_bolt: A bolt of Air: a fast projectile that strikes the first foe or wall it meets and bursts there.
nusmp.page.book_air.attribute_cut: A line of Air drawn straight ahead: it cuts through every foe along its length.
nusmp.page.book_air.attribute_field: A field of Air laid at the aimed point: it stays for a while and hurts everything inside.
nusmp.page.book_air.attribute_domain: The domain of Air: a great burst around you that throws back and hurts everything near.
nusmp.page.book_air.attribute_guard: A guard of Air: the magic wraps you and grants its protective effect for a few seconds.

item.nusmp.twin_hook_swords_left.desc: The left sword of a pair of hook swords. Right-click sweeps the leg of a two-legged or winged foe and drags it off its feet. Hold the right sword in the off hand: a second blow follows each strike, and the hooks hold you to a wall so you can climb.
item.nusmp.twin_hook_swords_left.card:
Normal Grade, the left sword of a PAIR of hook swords (the mirror of the right one): 3.8 damage, fast (2.4 attacks a second). Engravings: Swift, Sturdy. Pair: needs the other half. Hold one in the main hand and the other in the off hand: the off-hand sword adds a second blow of 60% of the first (own cooldown of 0.6 seconds), and the pair-only effects wake. One half alone keeps its abilities at a small penalty.
It carries every ability of the right sword (Sweep the Leg, the off-hand hook, the climb) and shares its cooldowns.
item.nusmp.whirling_blades_left.desc: The cold, cyan-bladed one of two curved swords that come as a pair: its blows chill. With the hot one in your off hand a second blow follows with its flame. Right-click joins their ends in a spin attack that hits everything around you.
item.nusmp.whirling_blades_left.card:
Rare Grade, the left (cold, cyan) sword of a PAIR of whirling blades: 5 damage, fast (2 attacks a second). Engravings: Severance, Swift. Pair: needs the other half. Hold one in the main hand and the other in the off hand: the off-hand sword adds a second blow of 60% of the first (own cooldown of 0.6 seconds), and the pair-only effects wake. One half alone keeps its abilities at a small penalty.
This blade's blows chill (Slowness and Tensura frost). It carries every ability of the right blade (the Spin Attack) and shares its cooldown.
item.nusmp.twin_swords_of_deflection_lef: The left one of a matched pair of hooked blades. With the right one in your off hand both land with each blow; a tenth of blows are critical, and the wielder is quicker. Use to parry: missiles turn back on their sender.

Needs attunement (set together with the right sword). Pair: needs the other half. Hold one in the main hand and the other in the off hand: the off-hand sword adds a second blow of 60% of the first (own cooldown of 0.6 seconds), and the pair-only effects wake. One half alone keeps its abilities at a small penalty.
The mirror of the right sword with all its abilities (Deflect, the crit, the speed) and shared cooldowns. 4.4 damage.
